title: My home
cando: describe your home, say where things are, and ask about a flat

about.text: In this lesson you talk about homes. You ask about a flat on the phone and say where things are. You read an advert for a flat. Then you describe a room so a friend could draw it.
goals: Ask about a flat: How many rooms are there? Is there a bath?
Say what is in a place: There's a shower. There are three rooms.
Say where things are: in, on, next to, behind, between.
Read an advert for a flat, and describe a room.
Phone about a flat, then describe your own home.

chapters.title: Asking about a flat
chapters.text:
In this lesson you talk about homes.
Carlos needs a flat. He sees an advert, and he phones the landlord.
He asks: How many rooms are there? Is there a washing machine? Where is the flat?
Listen for the answers. The rent is 750 pounds a month. The flat is on the second floor.

chapters.title: there is, there are
chapters.text:
To say what is in a place, use there is and there are.
One thing: there's a shower. Two or more: there are three rooms.
To ask, put is first. Is there a bath? No, there isn't.
To say where things are, use in, on, next to, behind and between.
The washing machine is in the kitchen, next to the fridge.
Between needs two things: between the bed and the window.

chapters.title: An advert for a flat
chapters.text:
Next, you read an advert for a flat.
Look for the rent, the floor and the rooms. What is in each room?
Then you describe a room in your home. Say what is in it and where.
Give numbers too: one window, two shelves.
Write it so a friend could draw the room.

chapters.title: Phoning about a flat
chapters.text:
Then you phone about the flat in the advert.
First, say why you are calling. I'm calling about the flat on Green Lane.
Ask five questions. Is there a washing machine? Is there a bus stop near the flat?
Last, describe your own home. How many rooms are there? What is in them?

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a short story about a home.
Read it once for the story. Then read it again and answer the questions.

warmup.prompt: You look for a new flat. What is most important?
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. For many people, the rent is most important. Other people want a quiet street or a big kitchen.

conversation.title: Asking about a flat
conversation.setting: Carlos needs a new flat. He sees an advert for a flat on Station Road. He phones the landlord, Mrs Mensah.
lines: Hello. I'm calling about the flat in the advert.
Yes, it's still free. What would you like to know?
There are three: a bedroom, a living room and a kitchen.
No, there isn't. There's a shower in the bathroom.
Yes, there is. It's in the kitchen, next to the fridge.
Where is the flat? Is it upstairs?
Yes, it's on the second floor. There's a garden downstairs.
And how much is the rent?
It's 750 pounds a month. Can you come and see it on Saturday?
Yes, I can. Thank you very much.

questions.why: Mrs Mensah says: There are three: a bedroom, a living room and a kitchen.

questions.a: in the kitchen, next to the fridge

Mrs Mensah says: It's 750 pounds a month.

items.meaning: The money you pay each month to live in a flat or house.
items.example: The rent is 750 pounds a month.

items.meaning: The person the flat or house belongs to. You pay the rent to this person.
items.example: I phone my landlord when something is broken.

items.meaning: About four weeks. There are twelve in a year.
items.example: I pay the rent at the start of the month.

items.meaning: One level of a building. Also the part of a room you walk on.
items.example: The flat is on the second floor.

items.meaning: On a higher floor of a building.
items.example: The bedrooms are upstairs.

items.meaning: On a lower floor of a building.
items.example: The kitchen is downstairs.

items.meaning: A place next to a house, with grass, flowers or trees.
items.example: There's a small garden behind the house.

items.meaning: You stand under it and wash. Water comes down from above you.
items.example: There's a shower in the bathroom.

items.meaning: A long, deep thing. You fill it with water and lie in it to wash.
items.example: Is there a bath in the flat?

items.meaning: A long, soft seat for two or three people.
items.example: There's a big sofa in the living room.

items.meaning: A machine in the kitchen. You make food hot on it and in it.
items.example: The cooker is next to the fridge.

items.meaning: A cold cupboard in the kitchen. Milk and meat stay cold in it.
items.example: There's some milk in the fridge.

items.meaning: A machine that washes your clothes.
items.example: The washing machine is in the kitchen.

sound.title: Questions that go up
sound.explain: Is there …? is a yes or no question. The voice goes up at the end. How many …? and Where …? are different. The voice goes down at the end. Listen, then say each group.
groups: Is there a bath? · Is there a garden?
How many rooms are there? · Where is the flat?

sayIt.instructions: Say Carlos's lines. Record yourself, then listen back. Does your voice go up after Is there …?
lines: Hello. I'm calling about the flat in the advert.
Where is the flat? Is it upstairs?
And how much is the rent?

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation. They say what is in the flat, and where.
examples: There are three: a bedroom, a living room and a kitchen.
There's a shower in the bathroom.
Is there a washing machine? Yes, there is.
It's in the kitchen, next to the fridge.
spot.question: When does Mrs Mensah say there is, and when does she say there are? Where does is go in the question? Which words say where the washing machine is?
spot.answer: There is (there's) + one thing: a shower. There are + two or more: three rooms. In a question, is goes first: Is there a washing machine? In and next to say where: in the kitchen, next to the fridge.

rules.title: there is, there are, is there …?
rule: One thing: There's a shower. There's a garden.
Two or more: There are three rooms. There are two windows.
No: There isn't a bath. There aren't any cupboards.
Question: Is there a lift? Yes, there is. No, there isn't.
How many rooms are there? There are three.
rules.mistake: Not: There is two bedrooms. Say: There are two bedrooms.

rules.title: in, on, next to, behind, between
rule: in: in the kitchen, in the cupboard
on: on the wall, on the second floor
next to: The fridge is next to the cooker.
behind: The garden is behind the house.
between: The desk is between the bed and the window.
rules.mistake: Not: The lamp is next the bed. Say: The lamp is next to the bed.

practice.q: ___ there a garden? Yes, there is.
practice.why: One thing, so the question starts with is.
Rooms is more than one, so are.

practice.q: Is there a bath? No, there ___ .
practice.why: The question has is, so the answer has isn't.

practice.q: The washing machine is ___ the kitchen.

practice.why: A picture is on a wall.

practice.q: The sofa is ___ the lamp and the window.
practice.why: Between has two things: the lamp and the window.

practice.q: The garden is ___ the house. You can't see it from the street.
practice.why: At the back of the house: behind.

yourTurn.prompt: Your friend is looking for a flat. Write five questions for the landlord. Use Is there …?, Are there …?, How many …? and Where …?
yourTurn.model: Is there a washing machine? Are there any cupboards in the bedroom? How many bedrooms are there? Where is the flat? Is it upstairs?

text.title: A flat on Green Lane
text.body:
PRACTICE ADVERT: this flat does not exist

TO LET: TWO-BEDROOM FLAT
28 Green Lane, Northfield

Rent: £900 a month
First floor. There is a lift.

Kitchen: a new cooker and a fridge
Living room: a sofa, two lamps, a big mirror and pictures
Bedroom 1: a double bed and a cupboard
Bedroom 2: a desk and two shelves
Bathroom: a bath and a shower

The walls are white. There are new carpets and curtains.
There is no garden, but there is a park next to the building.

No pets.
Call the landlord, Mr Adeyemi: 07700 900 789

gist.why: TO LET means you can rent it. The rent is £900 a month.

gist.q: Who do you call about the flat?
gist.why: The advert says: Call the landlord, Mr Adeyemi.

detail.why: First floor. There is a lift.
Bedroom 2: a desk and two shelves.

detail.a: No, but there's a park next to the building.
detail.why: There is no garden, but there is a park next to the building.

items.meaning: One side of a room. You can put pictures on it.
items.example: The walls in my flat are white.

items.meaning: A place with a door for plates, food or clothes. It is often on or next to a wall.
items.example: The plates are in the cupboard.

items.meaning: A long, flat piece of wood on a wall. You put books on it.
items.example: My books are on the shelf.

items.meaning: A table for work. You read, write or use a computer at it.
items.example: My desk is next to the window.

items.meaning: It gives light. You put it on a table or on the floor.
items.example: There's a lamp next to my bed.

items.meaning: A piece of glass. You look at it and see your face.
items.example: There's a big mirror in the bathroom.

items.meaning: A soft cover for the floor of a room.
items.example: The carpet in the bedroom is blue.

items.meaning: A photo or a painting. You often put it on a wall.
items.example: There's a picture of my family on the wall.

items.meaning: Long pieces of cloth at a window. You close them at night.
items.example: The curtains in my bedroom are green.

model.title: My bedroom
model.body:
My bedroom is small. The walls are white, and there's a blue carpet.
The bed is between the door and the window.
There's a lamp on a small table next to the bed.
My desk is next to the window. There are two shelves on the wall.
The cupboard is behind the door. There's a mirror on the cupboard door.
There are green curtains at the window.

write.task: Describe one room in your home, so a friend could draw it. Write five or six sentences, like the model. Say what is in the room and where each thing is.
checklist: I used there is and there are.
I used in, on, next to, behind or between four times.
I gave numbers: two shelves, one window …
I said where the big things are: the bed, the desk, the cupboard.

card.title: Phone about a flat
card.situation: You need a new flat. You like the advert for the flat on Green Lane. But the advert doesn't say everything.
card.goal: Phone the landlord and ask five questions. Then describe your own home: the rooms and what is in them.

phrases: Hello. I'm calling about the flat on Green Lane.
How many flats are there in the building?
Is there a bus stop near the flat?
Can I come and see it on Saturday?
In my home there are two rooms and a small kitchen.
prepare.notes: Read the advert again. Write five questions about things the advert doesn't say: a washing machine, a bus stop, the street, the neighbours. Then write three sentences about your own home.

doIt.liveClass: In the live class, your teacher is the landlord. Phone about the flat and ask your five questions. Then describe your own home: how many rooms there are, and what is in them.
doIt.wehel: You are the landlord of a flat on Green Lane. I am phoning about the flat. Answer my questions with there is and there are. Then ask me about my home now. Use simple English.

model.title: The phone call
lines: Hello. I'm calling about the flat on Green Lane.
Yes, there is. It's in the kitchen, next to the cooker.
How many flats are there in the building?
There are six. This flat is on the first floor.
Is there a bus stop near the flat?
Yes, there's one next to the park.
Yes, it's very quiet at night.
Can I come and see it on Saturday?
Yes, of course. Is ten o'clock OK?
Ten o'clock? Yes, that's fine. Thank you.
compare: Did you say why you are calling?
Did you use Is there …? and How many … are there?
Did you say the day and the time back to check them?

reading.before: Look at the title and the first picture. Where is the home? Who lives there, do you think?

quiz.why: A picture is on a wall.

quiz.why: You close the curtains at night.

quiz.q: This is Omar. ___ wife is a nurse.
quiz.why: Omar is a man, so his.
The brother of your mother or father is your uncle.

liveClass: Day 1: practise the phone call about a flat in pairs, then change the flat: more rooms, a garden, a bath.
Day 2: draw my room. One learner describes a room with there is, there are and in, on, next to; the others draw it, then compare.
Day 3: the phone call. You are the landlord. Each learner asks five questions about the flat in the advert, then describes their own home.
Day 4: talk about the book, answer questions, and let two learners read their room descriptions aloud while the class draws.
